the construction of mental simulations of future events is a protracted process that involves the retrieval and integration of general personal knowledge and that this general personal knowledge is mainly organized in the form of personal goals.

episodic future thought construction involves a protracted generality-to-specificity process, in which general personal semantic knowledge and anticipated general events provide a frame or context in which episodic details are retrieved, integrated, and interpreted.
episodic future thinking consists of transitory patterns that are generated from general personal knowledge structures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature of the mental representation that underlies the ability to imagine possible future events.
the nature of the knowledge structures that support future thinking.

the nature of mental representations of future episodes, and it suggests that episodic future representations are not static but dynamic, and that they can be understood as a dynamic pattern of activation over knowledge at different levels of abstraction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
episodic future thinking involves the retrieval, integration, and interpretation of personal semantic and episodic knowledge in the context of general knowledge about the future.
the episodic future thinking process is a dynamic process in which general knowledge structures are used to guide retrieval and integration of specific episodic details.

episodic future thinking involves a complex interaction of personal semantic information and episodic details, with the latter being retrieved and interpreted within a context provided by personal semantic information.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
episodic future thought consists of a dynamic pattern of activation over knowledge about the personal and episodic past, the personal future, and the episodic details.

episodic future thought is a dynamic process of retrieving, integrating, interpreting, and elaborating information from various sources, and that this process is organized around the individual’s current personal goals.
future thoughts consist of a network of transitory patterns, with personal goals as a central hub that connects the episodic and semantic components.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the construction of mental representations of possible futures may be more akin to the process of generating and interpreting stories than to that of retrieving and integrating memories.
the construction of future thoughts is an incremental, knowledge-driven process that is not limited to the retrieval of episodic details.
episodic future thinking should be considered as an extended process that involves the activation of knowledge structures at different degrees of specificity.
